editorial.headline: Living Aquatic Life Retail: Open Nationally, Blocked for Bali PMA
editorial.standfirst: Retailers of ornamental fish, aquaculture seed and other non-food live aquatic life can be fully foreign owned nationally, but Bali blocks PMA registration under its permanent risk-based moratorium.
editorial.body:
A foreign investor cannot register this activity as PMA in Bali today. That is the decisive local position for KBLI 47753, even though the activity is open nationally. Its scope is the retail trade of live fish and other living aquatic organisms not intended for consumption: ornamental fish, pearl oysters, sponges, milkfish fry, shrimp fry, fish seed and benih bening lobster (BBL). The common thread is that the product remains alive and sits outside consumption-oriented retail.

The code is available across every listed business scale: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar. In practical terms, it is the registration home for an operator whose retail activity consists of supplying these living aquatic organisms, whether the trade centres on ornamental specimens, cultivation seed or the other non-food live aquatic life named in the scope. The classification is therefore defined by both the retail setting and the living, non-consumption character of what is sold.

Nationally, the position is straightforward. The activity is marked TERBUKA, with a maximum foreign ownership of 100% under Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. Full foreign ownership is therefore available under the national framework. That national ceiling matters, but it is not a shortcut around a province-specific PMA restriction: the national openness describes the activity's position in the national regime, while Bali applies its own stated barrier to PMA registration.

Bali's status is BLOCCATO_CLASSE_RISCHIO. The stated reason is that, at the Besar scale, OSS risk is Rendah or Menengah-Rendah across every scope, bringing the activity within the Bali moratorium dated May 13, 2026. The provincial rule blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI activities for PMA on an island-wide, permanent basis. For this activity, the result is not a reduced foreign-ownership ceiling or a conditional route: PMA registration in Bali is blocked, despite the 100% national foreign-ownership ceiling.
editorial.pullQuote: National openness does not override Bali's permanent block on PMA registration for this activity.
